title: Microsoft Purview: sync status for sensitivity label publishing policies
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, portal navigation, PowerShell checks and Exchange Online retry guidance are supported. It correctly reports the difference between the roadmap's launched status and Learn's preview entry. The membership-removal guidance could include the final Remove members step.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters

claims.quote: You can now see the sync status of your sensitivity label publishing policies on the Label policies page, giving you visibility into when label policy updates are fully synced across Microsoft 365.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The new Label policies view is included within the licensing of the existing Microsoft Purview sensitivity-labeling product.
claims.quote: A number of different per-user subscriptions support sensitivity labels for Microsoft 365 apps and services, and the licensing requirements for users depend on the features you use. Admins also need a license to manage sensitivity labels.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The same service-description section says sensitivity labeling, including automatic or policy-based labeling, requires Microsoft 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 Information Protection and Governance (IPG).

claims.claim: The administrator creating and managing Information Protection features must have appropriate licenses.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Open questions
claims.claim: A portal control for retrying failed sensitivity label publishing-policy distribution is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview sensitivity label publishing policies retry failed distribution portal UI RetryDistribution; "sensitivity label" "RetryDistribution" portal retry. Opened Create and configure sensitivity labels and Set-LabelPolicy; portal Retry results cover retention, not sensitivity publishing.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: After rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy -Identity "<policy name>" -RetryDistribution is the documented retry operation.
claims.quote: Set-LabelPolicy [-Identity] <PolicyIdParameter> -RetryDistribution ... The RetryDistribution switch specifies whether to redistribute the policy to all Exchange Online locations.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: RetryDistribution redistributes the label policy to Exchange Online locations.
claims.quote: The RetryDistribution switch specifies whether to redistribute the policy to all Exchange Online locations. You don't need to specify a value with this switch.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls table
claims.claim: RetryDistribution is a separate parameter set of Set-LabelPolicy.
claims.quote: ## Syntax ... ### RetryDistribution ... Set-LabelPolicy [-Identity] <PolicyIdParameter> -RetryDistribution

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Locations whose initial distributions succeeded are excluded from the retry.
claims.quote: Locations whose initial distributions succeeded aren't included in the retry.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft advises running distribution retry only if necessary.
claims.quote: Because the process of retrying distribution is a significant operation, run it only if necessary and for one policy at a time.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft advises retrying distribution for one policy at a time.
claims.quote: run it only if necessary and for one policy at a time.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Distribution retry is not intended to run on every policy update.
claims.quote: It is not intended to be run every time you update a policy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; controls[2].note; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The Information Protection, Admins, Analysts, Investigators and Readers role groups grant sensitivity-label and label-policy portal permissions.
claims.quote: You can use the following role groups: Information Protection; Information Protection Admins; Information Protection Analysts; Information Protection Investigators; Information Protection Readers.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: A custom role group with Sensitivity Label Administrator can provide sensitivity-label administration permissions.
claims.quote: Alternatively to using the default role groups, you can create a new role group and add the Sensitivity Label Administrator role to this group.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Sensitivity Label Reader provides read-only sensitivity-label permissions.
claims.quote: For a read-only role, use Sensitivity Label Reader. ... These permissions are required only to create and configure sensitivity labels and their label policies.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The stated Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups > Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions > role group > Edit > Edit members of the role group > Choose users path reaches membership editing.
claims.quote: Go to Settings > Roles and scopes ... Select Role groups. On Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions, select a Microsoft Purview role group ... Select Edit ... On Edit members of the role group, select Choose users or Choose groups.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "<role-group>" -Member "<user-UPN>" adds the specified user to the role group and grants its effective permissions.
claims.quote: Add-RoleGroupMember [-Identity] <RoleGroupIdParameter> -Member <SecurityPrincipalIdParameter> ... When you add a member to a role group, the member is given the effective permissions provided by the management roles assigned to the role group.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Governance controls table; Governance controls prose
claims.claim: Managing role-group membership through the portal requires an admin account assigned Role management.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal ... by using credentials for an admin account assigned the Role management role.

claims.where: Governance controls: PowerShell rows
claims.claim: Get-LabelPolicy runs in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls table; Governance controls prose
claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy runs in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is functional only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.where: Governance controls: PowerShell rows

claims.where: Scope: What it covers
claims.claim: Sensitivity label publishing policies publish labels and policy settings to selected users and groups.
claims.quote: As part of the label policy, you select users and groups to have sensitivity labels and label policy settings.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft advises allowing 24 hours for labels and label policy settings to propagate before troubleshooting recent changes.
claims.quote: For labels and label policy settings, allow 24 hours for the changes to propagate through the services. ... it's a good idea to wait this 24-hour time period before you spend time troubleshooting labels and label policies for recent changes.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Changes depending on populating a new group or group membership changes can take 24-48 hours.
claims.quote: But for configurations that depend on populating a new group and group membership changes, or network replication latency and bandwidth restrictions, these changes might take 24-48 hours.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Neither the roadmap description nor the What's new feature entry describes reading or showing labeled content.
claims.quote: Searched: read the roadmap description and What's new May 2026 sensitivity-label sync-status entry. Both describe visibility into policy distribution; neither describes reading or displaying labeled content.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Neither the roadmap description nor the What's new feature entry describes the status view taking action on a policy.
claims.quote: Searched: read the roadmap description and What's new May 2026 sensitivity-label sync-status entry. Both describe visibility into completed policy sync; neither describes the view changing or acting on a policy.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, first bullet
claims.claim: The path ending at Edit members of the role group is the route given for reviewing membership and removing unnecessary read access.
claims.quote: On Edit members of the role group, select the check box for all users or groups you want to remove from the role group. ... Select Remove members, and then select Next.
claims.fix: For the removal instruction, extend the path to 'Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups > Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions > role group > Edit > Edit members of the role group > Remove members', after selecting the members to remove, as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/purview-permissions.
